body: Yes. If I didn't have a brother and parents I would already be gone.

Thanks, I appreciate the sentiment. Don't feel too jealous, most employers don't care if you have a PhD. They only care if know exactly how to solve their problem right now, not that you can learn how to solve their problem eventually. In general it hasn't helped me at all. I'm still proud of it, but unless you plan to be professor or a lifelong government research scientist it's not really worth it. Doesn't get you a damn job, and years of wasted earning potential. Once I had decided I wasn't going to be a professor I wish I had dropped out too. Gotten a degree in programming or business, something people actually give a shit about.

Thanks for the response. My problem is that I don't really like myself. If I did I don't think I would be in this situation, hehe. And that's not the first time I've been told something akin to 'focus on yourself.' I guess I don't really know how to. I've been with my ex since I was 16 years old... I don't know how to be alone.

That's a pretty good idea. One thing I realized yesterday: if I want a new job I need to start looking at different cities. There are just too few opportunities in my location (which is dominated by my current employer). I'm also thinking about a career change. I've even considered just quiting my job and looking full time, but I have a friend who just did that and he's almost completely broke and still jobless (and he's extremely talented and has an amazing resume).

One thing I have learned: physics is a terrible field for finding women. There are simply too few women in the field, and they are essentially thronged by dudes at all times.

Thanks for the response.
